newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end trade lower as dollar slides.
newsitem.headline: German shares end trade lower as dollar slides.

text.p: German shares ended thin bourse trade lower on Monday, taking a break after they reached record highs on Friday, with profit-taking and dollar weakness pressuring the market.
The dollar had fallen sharply under 1.51 marks on Friday, seen as negative for German exporters.
Dealers said weak volumes were partly due to the absence of some foreign players on holiday.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor dealings at a day's low of 2,728.32 points, down 11.51 points, or 0.42 percent.

The dollar continued to weaken after the bourse close, falling below 1.50 marks for the first time in two months, and weighing down the DAX in electronic trade, despite a firmer opening on Wall Street.
"The level of the dollar is an irritation for us," said one trader.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade in the DAX index, ended down 1.85 points, or 0.07 percent, at 2,730.44. The index had stuggled into positive territory, only to be pulled back after the dollar dipped under 1.5 marks.

Chemicals group BASF AG climbed in pre-bourse dealings after the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it conditional approval to market its Meridia obesity drug in the U.S..
But BASF later lost ground and ended IBIS trade down 30 pfennigs at 51.13 marks.
Drugs group Schering on the other hand, had lost ground in bourse trade, but ended IBIS dealings up 55 pfennigs at 125.40 marks, after the firm announced positive nine-month figures.
Dealers said a recommendation upgrade by a major investment bank had given the stock a late boost.
One of the day's biggest gainers was dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, which touched an IBIS year high of 148.95 and ended dealings up almost seven percent, or 9.40 marks, at 145.90.

Dealers said the stock was reacting belatedly to nine month results released on Friday, which had initially sent the stock down. "It was only by looking closely at the figures that you could see they were better than expected," said one dealer.

Meanwhile, state-owned telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, part of which is due to be floated next week, said it had topped up the volume of its share issue to 600 million shares or three billion marks from 500 million shares or 2.5 billion marks.
Dealers said the news had pushed down the price of Telekom shares in "grey" or unofficial pre-flotation telephone dealings, to 33.00 to 33.50 marks, from 34 marks.
